name: "Freezer Friendly" Green Tofu-Cheese Enchiladas with Bell Peppers & Onions (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes 2 (9 x 13-inch) baking pans of enchiladas or 8 servings.

FOR THE FILLING: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 red bell pepper
1 green bell pepper
1 yellow bell pepper
1 jalapeño pepper
½ small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into thin strips. Place in a large bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Small dice and add to the bowl with the bell peppers. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into ¼-inch thick strips. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, place spices in a small bowl and stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp chili powder
1 ½ tsp oregano, dried
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
¼ tsp cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and half of the spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until just fork-tender, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve large bowl and remaining spices for later use.)
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the veggies are done, return to the reserved bowl, along with cilantro. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)

Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Crumble tofu into large pieces with your fingers and add to the skillet, along with remaining spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tofu is warmed through and golden, 4-5 minutes. Transfer to the bowl with the veggies and cilantro.
instructions.secondary_message: 1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Add cheese to the bowl and stir to combine the filling.
TO ASSEMBLE THE ENCHILADAS: Coat two 9 x 13-inch disposable foil pans with a thin layer of oil.

Working in batches, warm tortillas in a microwave, oven, or skillet. Place warmed tortillas on a flat surface, then arrange a ⅓-cup of filling down the center of each. Roll up tightly and place, seam-side down, in the pans. Top with enchilada sauce, then sprinkle with additional cheese.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 (10 oz) can green enchilada sauce
shredded cheese, Mexican blend

instructions.primary_message: STORING: Tightly cover each pan with aluminum foil, then wrap the whole pan with plastic wrap. Place in the freezer for up to 1 month. HEATING: For best results, bake enchiladas from frozen, removing plastic wrap. Place foil-covered pan(s) in a preheated 375°F oven and bake until filling is heated through and cheese is just melted, 50-55 minutes. Remove the foil and continue to bake until cheese is golden and bubbly, 15-20 minutes more. Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before enjoying! (If you'd prefer to bake after assembly, place enchiladas in a preheated 350°F oven, uncovered, and bake until juices bubble and cheese is melted and golden on top, 40-45 minutes.)
